question.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)={y}^{3}z-xy+x{z}^{3}$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(2,-1,1).$
question.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(2,-1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{3}z-xy+x{z}^{3})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{3}z-xy+x{z}^{3})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({y}^{3}z-xy+x{z}^{3})\text{ }k \\  & =({z}^{3}-y)\text{ }i+(3z{y}^{2}-x)\text{ }j+(3x{z}^{2}+{y}^{3})k \\ ∇\,f(2,-1,1) & =({1}^{3}-(-1))\text{ }i+(3(1)(-1)^{2}-2)\text{ }j+(3(2)(1)^{2}+(-1)^{3})k \\  & =2\,i+\,j+5k \\  & =⟨2,1,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(2,-1,1)\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y+1,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨2,1,5⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y+1,\,z-1⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$
